Description: Subject intended learning outcomes for CSE5IDP Industry Development Project, Semester 2 2026, La Trobe University. Source: Subject Learning Guide and La Trobe Handbook 2026.

Short name: SILO1 Manage project meetings and progress
Description: Apply advanced skills and knowledge to effectively manage industry-based project meetings and progress.
Plan and run stand-ups, sprint planning, review and retrospective sessions that surface blockers early.
Maintain an accurate board and interpret burndown behaviour honestly, including explaining adverse trends.

Short name: SILO2 Apply specifications and standards to design
Description: Constructively consider specifications and the use of relevant standards to the design of software or network systems.
Decompose a project brief into user stories with positive and negative acceptance criteria, distinguishing user from system requirements.
State and measure performance, security, portability and reliability requirements rather than asserting them.
Align design decisions to a recognised framework such as OWASP Top 10, ASD Essential Eight or ISO 27001.
Develop and implement product prototypes following industry standard AGILE project methodologies.
Work in a shared repository with meaningful commit history, branching and no out-of-band code transfer.
Produce functioning, signed-off componentry each sprint rather than deferring integration.
Derive test cases from acceptance criteria before implementation and automate their execution.
Produce professional quality documentation to clearly articulate industry relevant outcomes.
Write system design and implementation reports that a reader outside the team can act on.
Produce a repository README, maintenance document and user guide sufficient for the project owner to run and maintain the system unaided.
Use professional oral communication skills to effectively convey industry applicable outcomes to expert and non-expert audiences.
Explain the product and its value to visitors without domain knowledge, as at the trade show.
Justify technical decisions and defend design trade-offs under questioning from the project owner and supervisor.
